questions.problem:
A partitioned matrix $M$ contains the following blocks: 

- ${M}_{11},$ which is a $3\times 3$ block

- ${M}_{12},$ which is a $3\times 2$ block

- ${M}_{21},$ which is a $2\times 3$ block

What are the dimensions of ${M}_{22}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We have a matrix of the form

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}{M}_{11} & {M}_{12} \\ {M}_{21} & {M}_{22}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3\times 3 & 3\times 2 \\ 2\times 3 & ?\times ?\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, ${M}_{22}$ must be a $2\times 2$ block.

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Block Diagonal and Block Triangular Matrices
questions.problem:
Which of the following matrices are block diagonal?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
A block diagonal matrix can be partitioned so that it has only square blocks on the main diagonal, and all the other blocks contain only zeros.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is *not* a block diagonal matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
\begin{aligned}A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- $B$ is *not* a block diagonal matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

- $C$ is a block diagonal matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$C$ only."

questions.problem:
Which of the following matrices are block lower triangular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
A block lower triangular matrix can be partitioned so that it has only square blocks on the main diagonal, and the blocks above the main diagonal contain only zeros.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is a block lower triangular matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- $B$ is a block lower triangular matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- $C$ is *not* a block lower triangular matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
\begin{aligned}C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ and $B$ only."

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Determinant of a Block Diagonal or Block Triangular Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we have  a block upper triangular matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}a & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & b & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}a & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & b & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}a & 2 \\ 0 & b\end{aligned}|\cdot 4 \\  & =-5\cdot 4 \\  & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we have a block upper triangular matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & x & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & y & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & x & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & y & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =6\cdot |\begin{aligned}x & -1 \\ 5 & y\end{aligned}|\cdot 5 \\  & =6\cdot (-3)\cdot 5 \\  & =-90.\end{aligned}
$$
